info.title: Votal Nexus API
info.description: One API for the web console, Nexus Mobile, the CLI and your own integrations. Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Errors use RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`.

token.description: Bearer token. Store securely; it is shown only once.

required.description: A second factor must be verified before the session is usable

enrollment_required.description: The org policy requires setting up MFA before continuing

choices.description: Three numbers; exactly one matches what the console shows

mfa_coverage.description: Share of active users with MFA, 0..1

mfa_policy.description: Who must enroll MFA. Users without a factor are asked to set one up at their next sign-in.

session_ttl_hours.description: How long a sign-in lasts before re-authentication

impact.description: What changes for people if this is applied

auto_apply.description: Whether 'Apply baseline' can fix this automatically

client_type.description: `public` for SPAs and native apps (no secret; PKCE required)

metadata_xml.description: The app's SAML metadata; fills entity_id and acs_url

attributes.description: Omit for the defaults (email, firstName, lastName, displayName, groups)

Sign in with email and password
post.description: Returns an active session, or a `pending_mfa` session when the user has MFA enrolled. A pending session can only call the `/v1/auth/mfa/*` endpoints.

post.summary: Complete sign-in (or step up) with a TOTP code
Revoke the current session

get.summary: The current session's sign-in state (works mid sign-in)
get.description: Lets a client resume a sign-in: `pending_mfa` → verify a factor, `enroll_mfa` → set one up, `active` → done.

get.summary: The signed-in user, their organization, roles and effective permissions
get.description: Clients use `permissions` to decide which actions to show. The server enforces them regardless.

post.description: Returns a secret and `otpauth://` URL to show as a QR code. The factor is inactive until verified.

Start pairing Nexus Mobile as an authenticator
post.description: Show `pairing_url` as a QR code. It is valid for 10 minutes and works once.

post.summary: Pair a phone using the code from the console (public; the code is the credential)
post.description: Registers the phone's Ed25519 public key as a push factor and returns a mobile session.

post.description: Show `number` prominently; the user taps it on their phone. Watch `/v1/me/stream` (event `challenge`) or poll the status endpoint.

Pending sign-in approvals for me

post.summary: Approve or deny a sign-in from the paired phone
Bulk import users from CSV (SPEC DIR-03)
post.description: Columns (header row, case-insensitive): `email` (required), `first name`, `last name`, `title`, `department`, `groups` (separated by `;`). Run with `dry_run: true` first to preview; nothing is written. Existing emails are skipped, never overwritten.

post.description: OIDC: confidential clients get `client_secret` exactly once. SAML: pass the app's metadata, or its entity ID and ACS URL; the response includes the IdP values to paste into the app.

get.summary: Apps I can launch
Authorization decision for the web tier
get.description: Used by the console's /oidc/{slug}/authorize handler, which attaches the signed-in user's session. Returns where to send the browser: back to the app with a code or error, to the Nexus login page, or to an error page.

get.summary: SAML sign-in decision for the web tier (SP-initiated)
get.description: The console's /saml/{slug}/sso handler forwards the SAMLRequest with the user's session and renders the result.

get.summary: SAML sign-in decision for the web tier (IdP-initiated, from the app launcher)
Pre-built SSO templates for common apps

post.summary: Add an app from the catalog
post.description: Returns the new app plus setup steps with the values to enter in the vendor's admin console.

get.summary: SSO signing keys and certificates

post.summary: Rotate the OIDC token signing key (requires recent MFA)
post.description: Apps that fetch JWKS pick up the new key automatically; tokens signed by the old key keep verifying until they expire.

post.summary: Start a SAML certificate rotation: create the next certificate (requires recent MFA)
post.description: The new certificate is added to IdP metadata but doesn't sign anything yet. Update apps that pin the certificate, then activate it.

delete.summary: Discard a pending SAML certificate rotation

post.summary: Finish a SAML certificate rotation: start signing with the next certificate (requires recent MFA)
Enroll a device (called by the Nexus agent)
post.description: Body `{token, device}`. The `NexusDevice` proof JWT carries the device's new public key in its `jwk` header.

post.summary: Report posture and inventory (called by the Nexus agent every minute)
post.description: Body `{device, posture, inventory?}`, signed with the device key (`kid` = device ID). Returns the next check-in intervals.

get.summary: List managed devices
Enrollment tokens

post.summary: Create an enrollment token (for MDM or manual installs)

get.summary: Device details: inventory and each policy check with the reason and fix

delete.summary: Remove a device: its key is no longer accepted and the agent stops reporting
Revoke an enrollment token (enrolled devices are not affected)

get.summary: My devices, with what to fix

post.summary: Get a one-time token to enroll one of my own devices
post.description: Valid for 24 hours and one device; the device is assigned to me automatically.

get.summary: Device compliance policies
get.description: Audit mode: devices are marked compliant or not and people are told what to fix; enforcement (blocking sign-in) comes from conditional access.

put.summary: Turn a policy on/off or change its settings; all devices are re-evaluated immediately
